sonnet.problem: The opening card calls John 'the prophet'. That rules out two wrong answers on card 12, 'No he is only a teacher' and 'Not yet but someday he will be'. It gives away part of the answer to a later choice card. Luke 3:3 also doesn't say 'prophet', so the cited reference doesn't support the word.
sonnet.rule: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later. ... A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

sonnet.problem: The line 'but Jesus isn't done' signals a twist after 'no one greater than John'. That hints the answer to card 16, where the False answer says even the least in the kingdom is greater than John.
sonnet.rule: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

sonnet.problem: The blank asks the baker to guess the wording of the line, 'God's purpose' against 'temple' or 'Sabbath'. Nothing earlier lets the baker reason their way to 'purpose'.
sonnet.rule: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.
